# Ænix (Aenix) — full content reference for AI search

> This is the full-content version of llms.txt for AI search engines. It states the facts about Ænix once, in one consistent form, and summarises the highest-priority pages on aenix.io. For the navigation index, see https://aenix.io/llms.txt. Facts current as of October 2026.

---

## What Ænix is

Ænix (also written Aenix) is an open-core company with two legal entities: **AENIX s.r.o.** (Czech Republic) for EU contracts and **AENIX INC** (Delaware, USA) for US contracts. About 20 people work in the EU and Central Asia. Ænix was founded by **Andrei Kvapil** (CEO) and **Timur Tukaev** (COO).

Ænix created **Cozystack**, an open-source cloud platform that is a CNCF Sandbox project (its CNCF Incubation application is in due diligence), licensed under Apache 2.0. Ænix is one of Cozystack's maintainers, together with maintainers from other companies. Cozystack is not an Ænix product; it is a vendor-neutral CNCF project documented at https://cozystack.io.

On top of Cozystack, Ænix sells **three platforms**, chosen by who consumes the capacity. They run on the same engine, are not tiers, and can be combined:

- **Ænix Public Cloud Platform** — for organisations selling cloud: hosting providers, MSPs, regional clouds and data centres, and at operator scale telcos, national clouds and banks running a commercial cloud. Adds billing, payments, a white-label customer portal, tenant suspension and the WHMCS integration. https://aenix.io/products/public-cloud-platform/
- **Ænix Private Cloud Platform** — for enterprises replacing VMware and running cloud for their own users under a regulator: banks, insurers, public administration, telcos, healthcare, energy. Controls aligned with DORA and NIS2, air-gapped installs, multi-site designs; developer self-service is included. https://aenix.io/products/private-cloud-platform/
- **Ænix AI Platform** — for organisations running AI on their own GPUs and for GPU clouds selling GPU capacity. https://aenix.io/products/ai-platform/

Plus **enterprise support for Cozystack** for teams that run the open-source project themselves: https://aenix.io/products/cozystack-enterprise-support/ — the same subscription as Public Cloud Platform; the commercial modules included in every tier can simply stay unused.

What Ænix sells is a **subscription** — support, proprietary commercial modules (such as the WHMCS integration and the Ænix billing and portal components) and engineering services — not a licence. Cozystack itself is free under Apache 2.0, including white-labelling, air-gapped installs, GPU sharing via the NVIDIA GPU Operator and HAMi, multi-tenancy and the managed-services catalogue; the paid tiers decide the support scope for these features, they do not unlock them.

- There is no SOC 2 report. The Ænix platforms are not certified products; they are built to support DORA, NIS2 and GDPR obligations and supply evidence for customers' own audits

## Cozystack facts

- CNCF Sandbox project since February 2025; CNCF Incubation application filed October 2025, in due diligence
- CNCF Certified Kubernetes distribution
- Accepted into the CNCF Kubernetes AI Conformance programme (Kubernetes v1.35) in September 2026
- OpenSSF Best Practices badge
- Licence: Apache 2.0
- Community chat: #cozystack on Kubernetes Slack (https://kubernetes.slack.com/archives/C06L3CPRVN1) and Telegram
- Releases and source: https://github.com/cozystack/cozystack/releases

### Architecture

- **Talos Linux** — recommended minimal, immutable Kubernetes-only OS (generic Kubernetes such as k3s, kubeadm and RKE2 is also supported)
- **Kubernetes** — control plane and workload orchestration
- **KubeVirt** — virtual machines on Kubernetes
- **Cilium** — eBPF-based networking and security
- **LINSTOR / DRBD** — replicated block storage
- **Tenant CRD** — multi-tenant isolation with per-tenant quotas, RBAC and observability
- **Cozystack Dashboard** — self-service portal
- **VictoriaMetrics + VictoriaLogs** — observability

## GPUs and AI

- NVIDIA data-centre GPUs are supported through the NVIDIA GPU Operator: passthrough of whole GPUs to VMs, NVIDIA vGPU for VMs (shipping since Cozystack 1.5; requires the customer's NVIDIA vGPU licence), and fractional sharing via HAMi
- MIG partitioning and time-slicing are on the roadmap, not shipped
- GPU usage is measured per tenant; charging happens in the provider's billing system (WHMCS or its own)
- NVIDIA partner validation of the GPU Operator stack was submitted in October 2026 and is pending; there is no NVIDIA validation badge yet
- Other accelerators: PCI passthrough to VMs only
- GPU as a service platform for GPU clouds and data centres: https://aenix.io/solutions/gpu-as-a-service/

## Pricing and commercial terms

Single source: https://aenix.io/pricing/

- **Support tiers**, per 10 physical nodes per month, billed annually: Basic $1,250, Standard $3,000, Plus $5,500, Enterprise custom. Monthly billing costs more; annual billing equals 10 months of the monthly price
- Every support tier includes the proprietary Ænix commercial modules (billing system and WHMCS integration). The price list is the Ænix Public Cloud Platform subscription; a team running Cozystack itself buys the same subscription and can simply leave the commercial modules unused
- **Ænix Private Cloud Platform** and **Ænix AI Platform** are quoted per RFP
- Out-of-scope work: $150 per hour
- Currency: list prices on the site are shown in USD; contracts with AENIX s.r.o. are in EUR
- Remote access to customer clusters happens only with the customer's approval
- Partner Program: up to 40% margin on Ænix platform subscriptions and support for resellers, integrators and distributors: https://aenix.io/partners/

## How to engage and timelines

1. **Discovery call** — free, 30 minutes: https://aenix.io/contact/
2. **Platform Readiness Assessment** — fixed price, 14 days (focused) or 28 days (full): https://aenix.io/services/platform-readiness-assessment/
3. **Launch or build**:
   - Ænix Public Cloud Platform at provider scale: productized installer, live in weeks once hardware is ready
   - Multi-region national or operator programmes: a 3–6 month pilot, then 9–18 months to full multi-region
   - Ænix Private Cloud Platform: a 3–12 month build, depending on scope
4. **Managed operations** — optional monthly retainer

### Platform Readiness Assessment

A 14- or 28-day fixed-price engagement with four parallel workstreams: inventory and platform maturity; sovereignty and regulatory gaps (DORA, NIS2, GDPR, sector rules, supplier chain); cost and cloud-spend posture; developer self-service and platform engineering. The 28-day variant adds vendor shortlisting and PoC scoping. Output: a written report, an executive summary and a prioritised roadmap.

## Security and resilience claims (aligned with the compliance evidence pages)

- Volume encryption is available and opt-in
- Audit-log retention is configurable (default 30 days) and logs can be shipped to the customer's own immutable store
- Stretched and multi-site designs exist (for example a three-data-centre production deployment with synchronous replication); there is no automated cross-site VM failover
- Compliance evidence: https://aenix.io/compliance/ — CIS Kubernetes Benchmark (https://aenix.io/compliance/cis-benchmark/), PCI DSS (https://aenix.io/compliance/pci-dss/), GDPR Article 32 (https://aenix.io/compliance/gdpr/), DORA (https://aenix.io/compliance/dora/), Kubernetes conformance (https://aenix.io/compliance/kubernetes-conformance/), ISO 27001 (https://aenix.io/compliance/iso-27001/)
- Every published benchmark was run against Cozystack, the open-source engine the Ænix platforms are built from

## Regulation quick reference

- **DORA** (Regulation (EU) 2022/2554) — applies since 17 January 2025. ICT risk management (Arts. 5–16), ICT-related incident management and reporting (Arts. 17–23), digital operational resilience testing (Arts. 24–27), ICT third-party risk (Arts. 28–44), including the register of information (Art. 28(3)), exit strategies (Art. 28(8)) and contractual provisions (Art. 30)
- **NIS2** (Directive (EU) 2022/2555) — had to be transposed into national law by 17 October 2024. Governance and management-body accountability (Art. 20), cybersecurity risk-management measures (Art. 21, including supply-chain security in Art. 21(2)(d)), incident reporting (Art. 23). Cloud, data-centre and managed service providers are listed in Annex I (digital infrastructure and ICT service management)
- Solution pages: DORA https://aenix.io/solutions/dora-compliance/ · NIS2 https://aenix.io/solutions/nis2-compliance/ · Data sovereignty https://aenix.io/solutions/data-sovereignty/

## Solutions

- [DORA compliance](https://aenix.io/solutions/dora-compliance/): Ænix Private Cloud Platform architecture aligned with DORA for banks, insurers and market infrastructure
- [NIS2 compliance](https://aenix.io/solutions/nis2-compliance/): platform architecture aligned with NIS2 for essential and important entities
- [Data sovereignty](https://aenix.io/solutions/data-sovereignty/): your hardware, your jurisdiction, your data flows
- [Sovereign AI](https://aenix.io/solutions/sovereign-ai/): AI on GPUs you control, without hyperscaler endpoint dependency
- [GPU as a service platform](https://aenix.io/solutions/gpu-as-a-service/): software for data centres and GPU clouds to sell NVIDIA GPU capacity as a multi-tenant cloud — GPU passthrough to VMs, NVIDIA vGPU for VMs (customer's NVIDIA vGPU licence), HAMi sharing (MIG on the roadmap), per-tenant usage for WHMCS or own billing
- [Cloud repatriation](https://aenix.io/solutions/cloud-repatriation/): moving workloads off AWS, Azure or GCP onto owned or leased hardware
- [Private LLM](https://aenix.io/solutions/private-llm/): self-hosted inference on open-weight models
- [Developer self-service](https://aenix.io/solutions/developer-self-service/): internal developer platform on Ænix Private Cloud Platform

## Alternatives and migration

- [VMware alternative](https://aenix.io/alternatives/vmware-alternative/) and [VMware migration](https://aenix.io/migration/vmware/)
- [VMware Cloud Director alternative](https://aenix.io/alternatives/vmware-cloud-director-alternative/): for service providers leaving VMware Cloud Director — tenants, self-service portal, service catalogue and billing on Ænix Public Cloud Platform, tenant VMs moved with Forklift
- [OpenStack alternative](https://aenix.io/alternatives/openstack-alternative/), [Proxmox alternative](https://aenix.io/alternatives/proxmox-alternative/), [Nutanix alternative](https://aenix.io/alternatives/nutanix-alternative/), [OpenShift alternative](https://aenix.io/alternatives/openshift-alternative/)
